# What's New in the GitHub Copilot App: Security Checks, Images, and Local Models

> **In short:** GitHub has announced a group of updates to its GitHub Copilot app. The most concrete is a security extension, now in public preview, that lets you work through code scanning alerts without leaving the app. Other updates cover images, local models, and work that spans several projects.

If you write code, manage a software project, or work with people who do, you may have seen the phrase "AI coding assistant" and wondered whether it has anything to do with your job. The updates GitHub just announced show where these tools are heading: they're less about one question and one answer, and more about helping with a whole piece of work.

## What GitHub announced

GitHub describes its Copilot app as a place where AI helps with software work. Its announcements cover five areas.

- **A security extension.** An extension is an add-on that adds features to an app. GitHub says this one lets you work through your repository's code scanning alerts without leaving the Copilot app. A **repository** (or "repo") is the project folder where code and its history are stored. A **code scanning alert** is a warning from an automated checker that a piece of code may have a security weakness. The extension is now in **public preview**, meaning people can try it now, though it's still being refined.
- **Smarter agents.** An **agent** is an AI that can carry out tasks, not just answer questions. GitHub says its agents should understand more than the code itself. They should also pick up on your team's preferences, repository conventions (the habits a project follows), and custom instructions (rules you set for how the AI should work).
- **Work across several repositories.** GitHub says real work doesn't always fit inside one project. A single feature can span several repos, and a launch plan can pull in specs (written requirements), designs, and assets without touching a repository at all.
- **Local model routing.** A **local model** runs on your own device. A **cloud model** runs on a company's remote servers. GitHub says Copilot Fusion can now choose between supported on-device models and cloud models. This routing is in **experimental preview**, which signals an early stage.
- **Image generation.** GitHub says you can now create and edit images in Copilot by describing what you want in everyday language. Your chosen **reasoning model** (the AI that works through a request step by step) calls a separate image tool to do the drawing.

## Why it matters

The common thread is context. Earlier AI tools often saw only the question you typed. These updates aim to give the AI more of the surrounding information: your project's history, your team's rules, and the related documents. GitHub's own framing is that agents should understand how your team works, not just what the code says.

The security extension is the most practical for teams today, because it turns a list of warnings into something you can act on in the same app. Still, GitHub's announcement describes it as a preview, so treat it as something to test, not a finished safety net.

## What this means for you

- **If you manage a software team**: Ask your developers which of these preview features they're testing before you plan around them. Check your organization's policies first, since new tools often need approval.
- **If you write or review code**: Expect warnings and suggestions to come with more background about your project. Read them with the same care you'd give a colleague's review.
- **If your work doesn't involve code**: Keep an eye on the image and planning features. Describing a launch plan or a design in plain language could become a practical way to start a draft.
- **If you're just getting started**: You don't need to understand every term above. Start by learning what a repository is and what a code scanning alert means. Those two ideas explain most of the security update.
- **If you already use it**: Try a preview feature on a small, non-critical project first. Compare what the tool flags against your own review. Note which suggestions you accept and which you reject; that record will show you where the tool helps most.

## Wrap-up

GitHub's announcements point toward Copilot working with more of your project's context, across more files and tools. The security extension is the clearest update to try right now, and the others are still in early stages or described only briefly. Your next step: open the GitHub Copilot app, or check GitHub's announcement, and find out which of these features are available on your account today.
